original_question: Classify the dynamics around a fixed point of a holomorphic map on P^k or even just defined in a neighborhood of p. -sibony@anh.matups.fr
target_in_paper: The unnumbered Dynamics/Scratchpad problem attributed to N. Sibony asking for a classification of the local dynamics near a fixed point of a holomorphic map of P^k, or more generally of a holomorphic map defined in a neighborhood of the fixed point p.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core mathematical target very well: it is about local holomorphic dynamics near a fixed point, it keeps the ambient several-complex-variables setting, and it preserves the paper's broad scope by mentioning both a global holomorphic self-map of P^k and the more local germ version near p.
missing_details: The ambient field should be stated explicitly: everything is over the complex numbers.
The fixed-point condition should be written explicitly as f(p)=p.
The global version should be stated as a holomorphic self-map f:P^k(C)->P^k(C).
The local version should be stated as a holomorphic map or germ f:U->X defined on a neighborhood U of p, with p in U and f(p)=p.
The symbol k should be quantified (typically k>=1).
The phrase "classify the dynamics" is too implicit unless one says that the object to classify is the local behavior of the iterates f^n near p.
It is not explicit whether the problem is qualitative/topological, holomorphic-conjugacy, or normal-form classification; this is left implicit in the draft.
The draft does not say whether one allows all fixed points, including attracting, repelling, neutral, resonant, and non-linearizable cases.
The draft does not specify which local invariants are meant to control the classification (at minimum the derivative Df_p and the nonlinear terms should be acknowledged).

Because the paper is a problem list rather than a theorem paper, the entry is not naturally sharpened by adding unrelated extra hypotheses such as degree bounds, invertibility, algebraicity, or genericity.
refined_question: Let k>=1, let p be a fixed point of a holomorphic map f, either globally as a holomorphic self-map f:P^k(C)->P^k(C) or locally as a holomorphic map (equivalently, a germ) defined on a neighborhood of p with f(p)=p. Classify the local dynamical behavior of the iterates {f^n} near p; in particular, determine the possible local dynamical types that can occur near p and how they are governed by the linear part Df_p together with the nonlinear terms.
justification: The paper is not a standard theorem/conjecture article but a bulletin-board style problem list. Its abstract explicitly says that some entries belong to a "Scratchpad" section for conversational or vaguely formulated questions, so the paper-faithful move here is to keep Sibony's problem narrow and close to its original local-dynamics wording rather than replacing it by a different, more formal neighboring problem. Within that format, your draft is already essentially on target: it asks for a classification of local dynamics near a fixed point for a holomorphic map on P^k, and it preserves the paper's own broadening to the merely local setting near p. What it lacks are the stand-alone details needed to state the problem cleanly: the complex ambient category, the explicit fixed-point hypothesis f(p)=p, the precise global/local domains, quantification of k, and the fact that one is classifying the local behavior of the iterates near p. Because this entry is an unnumbered problem-list item rather than a formal theorem, there is no paper-given equivalent reformulation to report.
